title: Comparability of random permutations in the strong Bruhat order
summary: The (strong) Bruhat order for permutations provides a partial ordering defined as follows: two permutations are comparable if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of adjacent transpositions that each increase the number of inversions by $1$. Given two random permutations, what is the probability that they are comparable in the Bruhat order? This problem was first considered in a 2006 work of Hammett and Pittel, which showed an exponential lower bound and a polynomial upper bound.
